messages:
maria: Heads up — support just escalated a customer report: sudden 401s + a token billing spike after last night's client generation run. They saw ~3x retries and duplicate charge traces.
ben: ugh. any repro steps? which language SDK?
alex: Python + TS clients. Customer is on redwood-client-python 1.5.2 and ts-sdk 0.9.7. They say behavior started after we pushed autogenerated clients from the new OpenAPI spec.
maria: support provided a minimal repro:
```bash
python -m pip install redwood-client==1.5.2
python -c "from redwood import Redwood; r=Redwood(api_key=\"REDACTED\"); r.chat.create(\"hello\")"
```
They also attached HTTP logs showing the header name mutated: server expects `Authorization: Bearer <token>` but client sent `Api-Key: <token>` in the new build.
ben: that's a schema change — did the spec rename the security scheme?
ci-bot: autogen: clients regenerated at commit abc1234 (openapi@refs/changes/feature/spec-optional-key). Diff summary: securitySchemes->apiKey header name changed from `Authorization` -> `Api-Key` for scheme `ClientApiKey`
alex: ok that explains 401s. But why double retries and billing spike?
maria: support trace shows client sees 401, triggers builtin retry (3 attempts), but servers were responding 401 quickly so each attempt consumed tokens counted by downstream billing hooks — customer saw 3x token counts in telemetry.
breakdown: first request returned 401, client retried with same malformed header 2x. No exponential backoff configured in generated client.
ben: we should hotfix two places: 1) patch generator to keep security scheme name consistent (Authorization header) and 2) push a patch to the runtime SDK to not auto-retry on immediate 401 for auth failures.
alex: quick diagnostic I ran locally: swapped the header in the TS client bundle and the call succeeds. minimal patch: map openapi securitySchemes->in:name fallback to `Authorization` if scheme type=apiKey & name looks like token.
support-ops: customer asked for ETA and asked us to revert to previous client build while we patch. They are on a tight billing contract.
maria: action items: @alex please open a hotfix PR to codegen mapping + add a test that regenerating against previous spec keeps header name. @ben please draft rollback note and coordinate with oncall to unpublish the broken packages. @ci-bot can you run a targeted bisect of autogen runs between abc0000..abc1234 to confirm exactly which commit introduced the schema tweak?
ci-bot: bisect queued — running regen pipeline for each candidate commit (this may take ~45m). Logs will be posted here.
alex: quick patch branch wip: fix-gen-security-header. I also added a guard: generated clients now treat 401 as non-retryable by default unless explicitly overridden. pushing PR now.
maria: please include repro unit: generate client from spec X, run simple request expecting header Authorization. Failing test should have assertion on raw HTTP header.
ben: for rollback: unpublish npm 0.9.7 and pypi 1.5.2, republish previous artifacts 0.9.6 / 1.5.1. I'll prep the release ops playbook.
support-ops: customer updated — they will pause traffic and wait for rollback. They asked for changelog transparency so we need clear release notes about the header mapping and retry behavior.
deploy-bot: Notice: package publish event: redwood-ts-sdk@0.9.7 published by ci-release (commit abc1234)
alex: thanks. I'll link the PR once CI finishes. If bisect points to the spec edit, we'll also reach out to the spec author to avoid silent breaking changes.
maria: really important: add a CI check that flags changes to securitySchemes (name/in/in) across spec diffs and blocks autogen until reviewed by API owners. That would have prevented this.
ben: agreed. I'll add it to the regen pipeline backlog item. :+1:
maria: logging note — let's add a short-term mitigation in SDK runtime: on 401 smoke after a publish, add telemetry that tags requests with client-gen-commit so we can quickly correlate future spikes.
support-ops: customer asked to be CC'd on incident updates — I'll keep them in loop.
alex: PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/client-gen/pull/482 (fix-gen-security-header). Included tests and updated changelog.
maria: great. once CI and bisect finish, we'll decide rollback vs patch release. thanks all.
